To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of an adaptive fuzzy control system allows two co operating mobile robot to successfully navigate through an unstructured environment, and that the use of a dynamic disturbance strategy within the fuzzy system increases the probability that the robot will successfully complete its mission.

a multi-layered fuzzy control architecture is an effective way to achieve a high degree of adaptability, and that the dynamic properties of a fuzzy rule base are an important factor in the adaptability of an autonomous system.

(i) a dynamic system can be used to achieve a state of adaptability in a multi layer control structure; (ii) the system can be made adaptive by introducing a disturbance to the system; (iii) the system can also be made to learn, by monitoring the activity of the fuzzy rules; and (iv) the system can then be made to learn by monitoring the activity and the state of the system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of an intelligent control system for co operating mobile robots.
the problem of maintaining a dynamic balance between conflicting reactive behaviours in an adaptive multi layer control architecture.
developing a model of a dynamic system which can be used to control a mobile robot in real time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of fuzzy rules to interpolate between reactive behaviours in a multi agent system, coupled with a mechanism for disturbing the control system to increase the probability of the system reaching its goal, is a viable approach to the design of autonomous agents in an unstructured world.

the proposed fuzzy system is capable of adapting to a dynamic environment, and that it can be further improved through the addition of a dynamic control system, which can be viewed as a disturbance of the fuzzy system itself.
a dynamic system is a complex system that is capable of self organization, self regulation, self control and adaptation to changing environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fuzzy system acts to control the relative importance of the reactive behaviours, and the rule vectors act as an adaptive mechanism which maintains the fuzzy system in a disturbed state.

the fuzzy system is used to balance the conflicting demands imposed on a robot by its environment and that this is achieved by using the system as a dynamic control structure which is maintained in a state of instability.

the system has a high degree of adaptability, but that this is not a result of a sophisticated model of the world, or of an exhaustive search of the state space, but rather of a simple mechanism for maintaining a state of disturbance within the control system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the control system itself should be considered an autonomous agent, with its own set of behaviours, and that the agent's behaviour should be considered as a result of the control system's behaviour.
the control system of a robot can itself be considered as an adaptive agent, with a set of internal states, which are modulated in response to external stimuli.
the use of an adaptive mechanism to control the behaviour of an autonomous system is not sufficient to achieve adaptivity.
